title: Inserting documents
summary: Add one or many documents to a collection with insertOne and insertMany.

options: A string of comma separated values
quiz.explain: `insertMany` expects an array, for example `[ { ... }, { ... } ]`. `insertOne` is the one that takes a single object.

quiz.q: Complete the method to add exactly one student.
You insert a document without an `_id`. What happens?
options: MongoDB adds a unique ObjectId as the _id
The document is saved with _id set to null
MongoDB uses the first field as the _id
quiz.explain: MongoDB generates a unique `ObjectId` for any document that does not bring its own `_id`.

quiz.q: One of these three lines fails when it runs. Which one?
quiz.code:
db.products.insertOne({ name: 'Pen', price: 10 })
db.products.insertOne({ name: 'Ruler', price: 20 })
db.products.insertMany({ name: 'Eraser', price: 5 })
quiz.explain: `insertMany` needs an array, so line 3 must be `insertMany([{ name: 'Eraser', price: 5 }])`. The first two lines correctly pass a single object to `insertOne`.

exercise.task:
The `products` collection already holds one product. Add three more:

- Use `insertOne` to add `{ name: 'Pen', price: 10, stock: 100 }`.
- Use `insertMany` to add `{ name: 'Eraser', price: 5, stock: 300 }` and `{ name: 'Ruler', price: 20, stock: 150 }`.

Prices and stock must be numbers.
hints: You need two statements, one after the other. The first adds one document, the second adds two.
`insertOne` takes an object. `insertMany` takes an array of objects, so use square brackets.
